html:
Zapotec Empire is the map's name for the Zapotec kingdoms of Oaxaca in southern Mexico in the late centuries before the Spanish conquest. After the great city of Monte Albán declined around 800 CE, power in the Valley of Oaxaca passed to several smaller Zapotec towns.

Zaachila became the leading royal seat, and Mitla the main religious centre, famous for walls covered in stone mosaics of geometric patterns. Zapotec lords also pushed southeast to the Isthmus of Tehuantepec.

They lived beside and mixed with the Mixtec kingdoms, sometimes as rivals, sometimes as allies by marriage. When the Aztecs pushed south in the late 1400s, the Zapotec king Cocijoeza held out at the mountain fortress of Guiengola; by tradition, peace was sealed by his marriage to an Aztec princess. The Zapotecs largely submitted to the Spanish in the 1520s. Their languages are still spoken today; see the Zapotec peoples.
